quests.sentenceWithBlank: They go to ___ church every Sunday morning.
quests.completedSentence: They go to church every Sunday morning.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Go to church' is a fixed institutional expression meaning to attend a religious service, so it takes no article, regardless of which building is actually used.
quests.nativeTip: This describes attending a religious service, not the building itself.
quests.example: They go to church every Sunday morning.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: We toured ___ church downtown because of its beautiful architecture.
quests.completedSentence: We toured the church downtown because of its beautiful architecture.
quests.ruleExplanation: Here 'church' refers to one specific, identified building being visited for its architecture, not the institutional sense of worship, so it takes 'the'.
quests.nativeTip: This time, you're visiting the actual building as a place to see, not attending a service.
quests.example: We toured the church downtown because of its beautiful architecture.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: My cousin got married in ___ small church near her hometown.

quests.grammarRule: Indefinite article before a consonant sound
quests.ruleExplanation: This is a new, not-yet-identified building being introduced for the first time, so it takes 'a' — 'small' begins with a consonant sound.
quests.nativeTip: This introduces a particular building for the first time, without identifying exactly which one for the reader yet.

quests.example: My cousin got married in a small church near her hometown.
